text:
Leo Carlsson scored in Utah on Saturday, then lasted about six minutes before an upper-body injury took him out of the game. CBS Sports lists him as day-to-day, and Inside The Rink noted the blow landed right after Beckett Sennecke went on injured reserve. Anaheim lost that night and again two nights later in Seattle without him, which tells you how much of this team runs through a 21-year-old.

The season has been a coming-of-age: 29 points in 24 games, 19 of them on the power play, at nearly 20 minutes a night. His speed numbers sit near the top of the league, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries last season, a setup man first. The caution is his finishing: he's shooting 17.5%, above the 12% to 17% range our numbers see as his true talent, and his last ten games produced 8 points against 11.2 expected. If the injury is short, the thing to watch is whether the power play keeps feeding him, because that is where his season has been built.
headline: Carlsson hurt as Anaheim's skid deepens
